files.release/fastlane/Fastfile:
default_platform(:ios)

platform :ios do
  lane :beta do
    increment_build_number(build_number: ENV["CI_RUN_NUMBER"])
    build_app(scheme: "Trailmate")
    upload_to_testflight
  end
end

platform :android do
  lane :beta do
    gradle(task: "bundle", build_type: "Release")
    upload_to_play_store(track: "internal")
  end
end

name: release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
jobs:
  build-ios:
    runs-on: macos-14
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.4.app
      - run: bundle exec fastlane ios beta
  build-android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: bundle exec fastlane android beta

from pathlib import Path

from trailmate_cli.gpx_import import read_points

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"


def test_naive_time_is_read_as_utc():
    points = list(read_points(FIXTURES / "naive_time.gpx"))
    assert points[0][2].endswith("Z") or "+" not in points[0][2]


def test_entity_bomb_is_rejected():
    import pytest
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        list(read_points(FIXTURES / "billion_laughs.gpx"))

fields.rule: never log raw GPS coordinates, user ids or push tokens; log a hashed id and the 2 decimal grid cell instead
never ship API keys or signing secrets in the JS bundle or in the app config; read them from CI secrets at build time

fields.purpose: opens the SQLite database and runs the numbered schema migrations on startup

fields.title: Store tracks and waypoints in SQLite, not AsyncStorage
fields.context: AsyncStorage stalled at about 4 MB of serialized tracks on Android (TM-118); SQLite holds 100k points and lets sync query by updated_at; tracks saved by older builds are imported from AsyncStorage on first launch

fields.title: Track the schema version with PRAGMA user_version
fields.context: a separate migrations table cost an extra read at cold start, while user_version is written atomically with the DDL, so a half migrated database is detectable

fields.rule: every schema change is a new numbered migration; never edit a released migration, and write a down step for each one

fields.title: App crashed on launch after the 1.7 update for users coming from 1.4
fields.root_cause: migration 5 added a NOT NULL column with no default and existing rows violated it, and the runner retried the migrate step in a loop (TM-163)

fields.fix_template: add the column nullable, backfill it in a second migration, then add the constraint
fields.caveats: SQLite cannot add a constraint in place, so rebuild the table inside one transaction and bump user_version last

fields.cases_required: upgrade from every released schema version to the current one on a fixture database, and a migration that throws leaves the old version intact

fields.description: the elevation profile is recomputed from track_points on every track open instead of being stored, about 400 ms for a 20000 point track; caching it in a column would need a migrate in db.ts

fields.title: Keep user preferences as one document per user on the backend
fields.context: units, map style and the set of alert regions sync as a single JSON document so a new phone restores them in one request, and the settings export for support tickets reuses the same document (TM-094)

fields.purpose: pushes the outbox in batches of 50 and pulls server changes since the last cursor; runs on foreground, on connectivity regain and every 15 minutes

fields.title: Resolve sync conflicts by comparing device timestamps
fields.context: simplest option and needs no extra server round trip

fields.title: Resolve sync conflicts by server updatedAt, last writer wins
fields.context: device clocks drift: TM-131 lost a 3 hour hike note when a phone clock was 2 days ahead; field level merge buys nothing because the waypoint editor only has name and notes

fields.title: Waypoint duplicated after a sync retry
fields.root_cause: the outbox row was only marked sent after the response was processed, so a timeout after the server committed sent it again (TM-142)

fields.fix_template: send the outbox row id as the Idempotency-Key header and have the server dedupe for 24 hours
fields.caveats: generate the key at enqueue time, never at send time, or a retry gets a new key

fields.reason: the API gateway config rejects bodies over 1 MB and a 50 row batch with track segments is about 600 KB

fields.name: sync_retry_loop
fields.signature: a failed push retried every 2 seconds with no backoff drains the battery and hammers the API on a flaky trail connection

fields.fix_template: exponential backoff starting at 2 s and doubling up to a 60 s cap with full jitter, reset after any success
fields.caveats: keep the cap in MAX_BACKOFF_MS, the fake timer tests rely on that constant

fields.description: NetInfo reports isConnected true on captive portal wifi, so check isInternetReachable before starting a sync; on Android it is null for the first second after launch

fields.solution: treat a null isInternetReachable as unknown and probe GET /health with a 3 s timeout
fields.description: only on cold start, afterwards trust the NetInfo event

fields.name: syncEngine.pullChanges
fields.frequency: on every foreground and every 15 minutes, so about 4 calls per active hour

fields.pattern: drive the sync engine with jest fake timers and an in-memory outbox; a test never sleeps for a real backoff or the runner hits its 5 s timeout

fields.cases_required: a timeout after the server commit does not duplicate, backoff caps at 60 s, and the queue survives an app restart

fields.title: Return API errors as one JSON envelope with status, code and message
fields.context: the client maps code to a localized string; before this each endpoint invented its own error shape and the app handled four of them (TM-070); the envelope schema lives in the shared API spec

fields.purpose: wraps the native location service; starts a foreground service on Android and enables background updates on iOS

fields.title: Sample GPS at 1 Hz while recording
fields.context: gives the smoothest line on the map

fields.title: Record a track point every 15 meters instead of every second
fields.context: 1 Hz filled 8 MB per 4 hour hike and cost 11 percent battery per hour in field tests (TM-097)

fields.description: iOS pauses location updates after about 10 minutes without movement when pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically is true, which split a lunch stop recording in two (TM-104)

fields.title: Background recording stops on Android 14 after 20 minutes
fields.root_cause: the foreground service had no foregroundServiceType location in the manifest, so the OS killed it (TM-151)

fields.fix_template: declare android:foregroundServiceType="location" on the service and request FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION
fields.caveats: Play Console needs the foreground service declaration form filled before the release is approved

fields.rule: drop fixes with horizontal accuracy worse than 30 m before writing them to the track

fields.reason: single row writes took 4 ms each and blocked the JS thread while recording

fields.description: the recorder keeps its buffer in a module level variable, so two recordings cannot run together; it needs a session object

fields.name: gps_spike
fields.signature: one fix jumps 200 m or more and comes back, inflating distance and elevation gain in the track stats

fields.fix_template: reject a point that implies more than 12 m/s from the previous one, then smooth elevation with a 5 point median
fields.caveats: cycling mode raises the speed limit to 25 m/s

fields.rule: use console.log with a [tm] prefix for diagnostics
use the logger module with levels; debug logs are stripped from release builds and warnings become Sentry breadcrumbs

fields.description: iOS background fetch fires every 15 minutes, so the alert refresh can rely on that interval

records.retracted: iOS schedules fetches opportunistically; the interval was measured at 15 minutes to several hours

fields.purpose: single entry for requesting location and notification permissions; exposes granted, denied or blocked to the screens

fields.title: Ask for foreground location first and background only when the user starts a recording
fields.context: onboarding experiment TM-089 got 71 percent opt-in with the staged ask and 38 percent with Always up front

fields.rejected_because: App Review rejected build 1.4 under guideline 5.1.1 because the purpose string did not explain background use

fields.rule: show the in-app rationale screen before any system permission prompt, because iOS only lets you ask once

fields.title: Permission prompt shown in a loop after the user chose Don't ask again on Android
fields.root_cause: the gate handled blocked like denied and requested again; the request resolves instantly with no dialog, so the screen re-rendered forever (TM-160)

fields.fix_template: on blocked, route to a screen that calls Linking.openSettings and re-check the state when AppState becomes active
fields.caveats: never call request again, Android returns immediately

fields.purpose: registers the FCM token, creates the Android channels and routes a tapped notification to its deep link

fields.title: Use FCM for both iOS and Android push delivery
fields.context: one server process and one Firebase config per build flavor instead of two integrations; the APNs key is uploaded to the Firebase console and the legacy GCM keys were migrated in the same change (TM-076)

fields.title: Weather alerts stopped arriving after an app reinstall
fields.root_cause: the server log showed UNREGISTERED for the old FCM token because the new one was only sent on login; tokens are now re-registered on every cold start when they differ (TM-166)

fields.description: Android 8+ ignores sound and importance changes once a channel exists; set them on a new channel id, hence trail-alerts-v2

fields.rule: push payloads carry only a deep link and a title; the app fetches the body on open so no trail location leaves the server inside a notification

fields.question: Can a silent push wake iOS to refresh an alert region while the app is force quit? Apple docs say no but we have not measured it

fields.purpose: wraps react-native-iap: loads the Pro products, starts a purchase and finishes the transaction once the server confirms

fields.title: Validate store receipts on our server, never trust the device
fields.context: a jailbroken test phone unlocked Pro offline in TM-125; the server process checks with Apple and Google before it sets the entitlement

fields.title: Pro users charged but not upgraded on slow Android payment methods
fields.root_cause: Play returns PENDING for cash based payments; the code treated any non-error result as purchased and finishTransaction was never reached (TM-172)

fields.fix_template: handle PENDING separately: grant Pro only when purchaseState is PURCHASED, keep PENDING ones in a local list and re-check them when the app returns to the foreground
fields.caveats: acknowledge within 3 days or Google refunds the purchase

fields.cases_required: a pending purchase does not grant Pro, a duplicate transaction id is ignored, and a refunded entitlement is revoked on the next sync

fields.title: Price shown with the wrong currency symbol
fields.root_cause: the localized price string was cached across a locale change

records.retracted: could not reproduce on a physical device; it was a simulator locale setting

fields.purpose: disk cache for raster map tiles keyed by z/x/y with LRU eviction

fields.title: Cap the tile cache at 500 MB with LRU eviction
fields.context: low end Android phones with 32 GB showed the app at 3 GB in settings (TM-109); 500 MB holds about 60000 tiles at 8 KB

fields.title: Gray squares on the map after the app was killed mid download
fields.root_cause: a tile was written straight to its final path, so a kill left a truncated PNG (TM-137)

fields.fix_template: write to <name>.tmp, then rename it; on startup delete any leftover .tmp files
fields.caveats: rename is atomic only within one volume, so keep the tmp file next to the cache

fields.purpose: lets a user download a rectangle of tiles for zoom 10 to 16 and tracks progress in a download queue

fields.title: Allow offline regions up to 50000 tiles
fields.context: covers a whole national park in one download

fields.title: Limit an offline region to 20000 tiles
fields.context: a user picked a whole country at zoom 16 and the queue ran for 9 hours; 20000 tiles is about 160 MB, enough for one hike area (TM-122)

fields.name: Serial tile download queue
fields.why_chosen: one worker with 4 parallel requests stays under the tile provider's limit of 10 requests per second

fields.description: the tile server returns the same ETag after a map data update because it hashes the URL, so ETag revalidation never refreshes a tile

fields.solution: treat tiles older than 30 days as stale and fetch them again
fields.description: until the provider fixes its ETags (PRV-4412)

fields.purpose: initialises Sentry, names releases trailmate@version+build and keeps the last 50 breadcrumbs; the settings screen offers a log export for support tickets

fields.title: Use Sentry for crash reporting instead of Crashlytics
fields.context: one project covers JS and native crashes and takes Hermes source maps, while Crashlytics lost symbolication for Hermes bytecode (TM-081)

fields.rule: the Sentry release string is trailmate@<version>+<build>, built by releaseName() for both the app and the source map upload

fields.title: Crash stack traces unreadable for build 1.6.2
fields.root_cause: source maps were uploaded under release 1.6.2 but the app reported 1.6.2+412, so Sentry found no match (TM-155)

fields.fix_template: derive the release string in one function used by both the upload step and init
fields.caveats: the upload script must import releaseName from reporter.ts instead of copying the format, and the CI step must read the build number from the same env var Fastlane uses

fields.operation: cold start to first map frame
fields.reason: initialising the crash reporter eagerly added 340 ms, so it is deferred until after the first render

fields.name: hermes_date_parse
fields.signature: Hermes cannot parse an ISO date with a space instead of T, so the sync cursor came back NaN

records.retracted: the cause was a malformed cursor from the server (TM-139), not Hermes

fields.title: Write the CLI in Python with click, not in Node
fields.context: the data team already uses Python for GPX tooling and the CLI shares no code with the app (TM-064)

fields.purpose: exports tracks from the Trailmate API to GPX 1.1 or GeoJSON
reads GPX files, validates them and uploads the tracks and waypoints

fields.title: Export GPX 1.1 with Trailmate fields inside the extensions block
fields.context: Garmin and Komoot importers drop unknown elements outside extensions, so pace and elevation gain go inside it (TM-113)

fields.title: GPX import froze the CLI on a hostile file
fields.root_cause: the stdlib XML parser expanded nested entities in a 40 KB billion laughs document (TM-148)

fields.fix_template: parse with defusedxml and reject files over 20 MB before reading them
fields.caveats: the size check goes first, defusedxml alone still loads a huge but valid document

fields.name: gpx_naive_time
fields.signature: time elements without a Z suffix are read as local time, so an export then import round trip shifts the track by the importer's UTC offset

fields.fix_template: read a time without an offset as UTC, as the GPX spec requires, and warn once per file
fields.caveats: some watches write local time; offer an --assume-tz flag rather than guessing

fields.operation: GPX import of a large file
fields.constraint: stream with iterparse and stay under 200 MB of memory for a 20 MB file
fields.reason: building the full tree used 1.4 GB on a 12 MB multi-day document and the CLI was killed

fields.preferred_form: raise click.ClickException with a one line message so a failed export exits with code 2
fields.avoid: printing a traceback to the user

fields.pattern: GPX tests use the files in tests/cli/fixtures and assert on parsed points, not on raw XML strings

fields.state: the time plus lat plus lon key is done, the 1 second tolerance for near duplicate points is not started

fields.purpose: lanes: beta uploads to TestFlight and the Play internal track, release promotes with a phased rollout

fields.title: Roll out store releases in phases of 5, 20, 50 and 100 percent
fields.context: a bad 1.5.0 reached every user within 3 hours and the crash free rate fell to 94 percent (TM-101); the rollout steps are in the release runbook document

fields.rule: the build number comes from the CI run number; never set versionCode or CFBundleVersion by hand or in the app config

fields.title: iOS archive failed on the macOS runner after an Xcode update
fields.root_cause: the build log showed the runner image moved to a newer Xcode and the pinned CocoaPods could not build with it; the image and Xcode path are now pinned (TM-170)

fields.fix_template: pin the runner to macos-14 and select Xcode 15.4 with xcode-select before the pod install
fields.caveats: revisit when GitHub retires the macos-14 image

fields.description: Play Console rejects a bundle whose versionCode is not higher than any track, even one from a rejected release; bump the build before retrying

fields.option: move release builds to Expo EAS Build
fields.rejected_because: the native location modules need custom config plugins and free tier queue times ran 40 minutes
